items.description: A table whose rows trade places. Sorting keeps every row's key and FLIPs it to its new seat on glide instead of re-painting the body, so a reorder is something the eye can follow; the header's arrow flips on snap and the sorted column tints. Headers are buttons inside th cells carrying aria-sort — the first press sorts ascending, the second reverses, the third clears back to the source order.

props.name: columns
props.description: Columns, left to right; numeric ones sort by value and right-align in a mono tabular face.

props.name: rows
props.description: Rows as plain records, each carrying a stable key field the FLIP animation tracks.

props.name: sort / defaultSort
props.description: Controlled or initial sort; null is the source order.

props.name: onSortChange
props.description: Fires with the new sort, or null when a third press clears it.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats a cell — numbers should come through here rather than raw.

props.name: rowKey
props.description: Row field holding the stable key; rows keep it across sorts so they travel rather than blink.

props.name: label
props.description: Table caption, read by assistive technology and hidden on screen.

usageNotes: Each header is a button inside a th carrying aria-sort: press to sort ascending, again to reverse, a third time to clear; Enter and Space activate it like any button and the new order is announced.
Rows animate with layout="position" so only the seat change moves — a full layout animation would scale-correct cells that never resized.
Under reduced motion the rows simply swap: the order still changes, because the order is the information.
Sorting never changes a header's width — the arrow is always rendered and only its opacity and rotation change.

items.title: Waterfall Steps
items.tagline: Each bar starts where the last one ended.
items.description: A cash bridge that builds itself. Every bar grows from the running total the last one ended on, in cascade() order on glide, with rises drawn in success, falls in danger and hairline connectors drawing between them on flick; the closing bar lands on recoil, two visible bounces for the arrival the chart was building toward. Columns are a list of buttons: hover or focus reads a step's delta and running total, Left and Right walk them, Home and End jump to the totals.

props.name: steps
props.description: Ordered changes between the opening and closing totals; a negative delta falls.

props.name: start
props.description: Opening value the first step builds on.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats every number: the rolling readout, the caption total and the aria text.

props.name: height
props.description: Plot height in px. The width is fluid and measured, so the columns fit any container.

props.name: label
props.description: Chart name; also the caption above the plot, opposite the closing total.

props.name: startLabel / totalLabel
props.description: Column names for the two total bars.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.description: Fires with the column index under the pointer or focus, or null when it clears.

usageNotes: Columns are list items holding buttons with aria-labels that read the delta and the running total: Left and Right walk the columns on a roving tabindex, Home and End jump to the opening and closing totals.
The hover readout is absolutely placed and clamped inside the plot, and its digits roll from motion values, so reading the chart never moves the page.
Under reduced motion the bars appear in place and the connectors are already drawn — the values still arrive, because the values are the information.
Bars animate their y and height attributes rather than scaleY, so no transform-origin rewrite is involved and the corner radii never stretch.

items.title: Range Histogram
items.tagline: Drag the thumbs; the bars outside fade.
items.description: A price filter you can see through. A histogram of the whole population sits above a dual-thumb range, and dragging a thumb fades every bin outside the selection on a plain opacity tween while the match count rolls to its new figure from a motion value on glide. The thumbs are real sliders carrying aria-valuetext: arrows step, Shift steps ten, Home and End run to the ends, and a thumb pushes its partner rather than crossing it.

props.name: bins
props.description: Ordered bins, left to right; their outer ends set the slider's bounds.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial range; it defaults to the full span of the bins.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires on every drag frame and every keyboard step.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats the two ends and the sliders' aria-valuetext.

props.name: step
props.defaultValue: a quarter of the narrowest bin
props.description: Arrow-key step; Shift and the page keys move ten of them.

props.name: height
props.description: Histogram height in px. The width is fluid and measured.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the filter for assistive technology and captions the match readout.

usageNotes: Two role=slider thumbs with aria-valuetext: Left and Right step, Shift or the page keys step ten, Home and End run to the ends, and each thumb's aria-valuemax or valuemin is its partner, so they never cross.
A press on the track moves the nearest thumb and captures the pointer only after 4px of travel, so a plain click is never swallowed and a synthetic sweep cannot throw.
A bin counts as selected when its midpoint falls inside the range, so the fade and the match count always agree.
Under reduced motion the bins swap state with no fade and the count sets instantly — the selection still shows, because the selection is the information.

items.title: Diff Lines
items.tagline: The old line strikes; the new one types in.
items.description: An inline word diff you can read and apply in place. Removed words fade to a ghost while a strike draws through each one with pathLength on flick, added words wipe in from the left on a clip tween under a success wash that cools over a second, and accepting a hunk drops its ghost on the exit ease while the measured passage glides to its new height. Each accept is a real toggle button, so Tab reaches it and Enter or Space applies the change or puts it back; arrows move between the change and result stops.

props.name: before
props.description: The original text; the diff is computed by word.

props.name: after
props.description: The edited text; the diff is computed by word.

props.name: view / defaultView
props.description: Whether the passage shows the change or the result.

props.name: onViewChange
props.description: Fires when the view switch moves.

props.name: onAccept
props.description: Fires when a hunk is accepted.

props.name: onAcceptedChange
props.description: Fires whenever the accepted set changes, restores included.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label above the passage.

usageNotes: Tab reaches every accept toggle; Enter or Space applies a hunk and applies it again in reverse. The view switch is a radio group: arrows move, Home and End jump, Space selects.
Under reduced motion the spans swap — the strike is already drawn and the new wording is already in place, because the change is the information.
The passage's height is measured with a ResizeObserver and glided, so no room is held for the longer of the two texts.

items.title: Fold Text
items.tagline: The clamp lets go; the fade lifts.
items.description: Read-more done by measurement. The folded box is exactly as many line boxes tall as it claims, and opening animates that height to the content's ResizeObserver-measured height on glide while the bottom fade lifts on an opacity tween and the chevron snaps over with the label. It is a real disclosure button: aria-expanded and aria-controls, Enter or Space to open, and no button at all when the passage already fits.

props.name: lines
props.description: Visible lines while folded.

props.name: children
props.description: The text.

props.name: moreLabel
props.description: Button copy while folded.

props.name: lessLabel
props.description: Button copy while open.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial open state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires when the disclosure opens or folds.

usageNotes: A disclosure button with aria-expanded and aria-controls: Tab reaches it, Enter or Space folds and unfolds the region it names.
Under reduced motion the heights swap and only the fade tweens — the text still arrives, because the text is the information.
Nothing is reserved: the folded height comes from the line box, the open height from a ResizeObserver, and a passage that already fits shows no button.

items.title: Gloss Word
items.tagline: Hover the term; the gloss unfolds inline.
items.description: A glossary term that explains itself without covering the sentence. Hover, focus or tap unfolds the gloss on the line beneath and pushes the following text down on glide, over a height a ResizeObserver measures rather than reserves; bubble mode floats it above instead, entering on snap from 4px and clamped to its paragraph. The term is a real button with aria-expanded and aria-controls, so Enter or Space toggles it and Escape closes it.

props.name: term
props.description: The word as it reads in the sentence.

props.name: gloss
props.description: The explanation.

props.name: mode
props.description: Whether the gloss unfolds beneath the line or floats above it.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires when the gloss opens or closes.

usageNotes: The term is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls: Tab reaches it, Enter or Space toggles the gloss, Escape closes it, and a pointer leaving closes it too.
Under reduced motion the gloss appears in place — no unfold, no travel — because the explanation is the point.
The inline gloss is a full-width float, so give the paragraph that holds the terms `display: flow-root` and it will contain every gloss it opens.

items.title: Find Marks
items.tagline: Type, and the matches light up in order.
items.description: Find in text, with the finding visible. Every match takes a wash that sweeps in from its left edge on a cascade capped at the 600ms budget, and one ring travels between matches on glide through a shared layoutId so the reader follows a ring that moves rather than one that blinks. Enter steps forward, Shift+Enter steps back, and the counter rolls a digit at a time on snap.

props.name: text
props.description: The body to search.

props.name: query / defaultQuery
props.description: Controlled or initial search term.

props.name: onQueryChange
props.description: Fires on typing.

props.name: caseSensitive
props.description: Match case.

props.name: onMatchChange
props.description: Fires when the current match or the total changes; memoise it.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Tallest the passage grows before it scrolls, in px.

props.name: label
props.description: Field label, used as the accessible name.

usageNotes: The field is a searchbox: Enter steps to the next match, Shift+Enter to the previous, and the same steps sit beside it as buttons with labels for a pointer.
Under reduced motion the marks appear and the ring cuts to its match — the highlight and the count are information, so they still show.
The passage scrolls itself rather than the document, so stepping through matches never drags the page.

items.title: Select Bar
items.tagline: Select words; the bar rises above them.
items.description: A format bar that rises out of the selection. Selecting words lifts the toolbar above them on recoil, positioned from the selection's own rectangle and clamped to the passage; it glides sideways when the selection moves and fades on the exit ease when it collapses. Formatting is range wrapping rather than execCommand, and the bar is a role=toolbar with a roving tabindex where Left and Right step the buttons and Escape drops it.

props.name: actions
props.description: Buttons on the bar.

props.name: children
props.description: The editable content; it is seeded once and then owned by the editor.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fires after an action, with the editor's HTML.

props.name: onAction
props.description: Fires with the action that was applied.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the editable region.

usageNotes: The editor is a textbox reachable by Tab; the bar is a toolbar with a roving tabindex — Left and Right step the buttons, Home and End jump, Enter or Space applies, Escape drops the bar. Cmd or Ctrl with B or I never needs the bar at all.
Under reduced motion the bar appears where it belongs instead of rising, and still follows the selection.
Formatting wraps the live range in real elements, so the HTML handed to onChange is the markup a reader would expect: strong, em, a, code.

items.title: Mention Chip
items.tagline: Type @, pick a name; it becomes a chip.
items.description: A composer that turns names into chips. Typing @ opens a listbox under the field that filters as you type, and choosing inflates the word in place — scale from 0.9 on snap with the colour wash arriving as a tween underneath — while Backspace against a chip's trailing edge fades the whole mention out before the characters go, so the line never reflows out from under the fade. The field is a real textarea with a painted layer behind it, so the caret, the selection and every native editing shortcut survive; focus stays in the text and aria-activedescendant drives the list, where Up and Down move the highlight, Enter or Tab inserts and Escape dismisses. Under reduced motion the chip simply appears.

props.name: people
props.type: { id: string; name: string; handle: string }[]
props.description: Who can be mentioned. Name and handle are both searched.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Composer content. Mentions are ids, recomputed from the text on every edit.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fires on every edit with the text and the ids mentioned in it.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Empty copy, painted in the field and set on the textarea.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible field label. Omit it and pass aria-label to label the field invisibly.

usageNotes: Type @ to open the list: Up and Down move the highlight, Enter or Tab inserts the mention, Escape dismisses it. Backspace at a chip's trailing edge (or Delete at its leading edge) removes the whole mention.
Under reduced motion the chip appears rather than inflating, and a removed mention leaves without the fade.
A mention stores the space inside a name as a non-breaking one so the textarea and the painted layer wrap identically — read value.text back with that in mind.

items.title: Squiggle Mark
items.tagline: The squiggle draws under the doubt.
items.description: Spellcheck marks that behave like a proofreader. A wavy path draws under each flagged word with pathLength on flick — a mark is a note, not an event — staggered by cascade so a paragraph's worth lands inside the choreography budget, and hovering or focusing a word raises its suggestion. Accept swaps the word, the old copy fading while the new one enters from a nudge, and retracts the squiggle back along its own path; Ignore leaves the word and dissolves the mark. Every flagged word is a button described by its suggestion, so Tab reaches the word, then Accept and Ignore, Escape closes the bubble, and resolving one hands focus to the next open word. Under reduced motion the squiggles are simply there.

props.name: text
props.description: The sentence to mark up. Flagged words are matched inside it in order.

props.name: issues
props.description: Flagged words and their fixes, in the order they appear in the text.

props.name: onFix
props.description: Fires on accept with the replacement, or on ignore with null.

usageNotes: Tab reaches each flagged word, which opens its bubble; Tab again lands on Accept then Ignore, Escape closes the bubble, and resolving a word moves focus to the next flagged one.
Under reduced motion the squiggles appear complete, the replacement swaps without travel, and the mark clears instead of retracting.
The bubble is measured against the text block and clamped to it, and drops below a word on the first line so it never leaves the column.

items.title: Karaoke Line
items.tagline: Words light in time; the caret glides ahead.
items.description: A line that lights in time. Each word fills with colour as its window passes — a clip sweeping across the glyphs on a linear tween scaled to that word's own duration, because a fill is a measurement and measurements do not ease — while the word being sung inflates 4% on snap and a soft caret glides ahead on glide, riding the trailing edge of the live word and slipping to the leading edge of the next one through a gap. The clock is either yours through time or the component's through playing, and it never starts on mount. Words are buttons in a roving tabindex: Left and Right walk the line, Home and End jump to its ends, Enter or Space seeks. Under reduced motion the words switch colour at their moment, with no inflate and no travelling caret.

props.name: words
props.type: { text: string; start: number; end: number }[]
props.description: The line in timing order; start and end are seconds.

props.name: time
props.description: Controlled playhead in seconds. Omit it to use the internal clock.

props.name: playing
props.description: Runs the clock at 20 ticks a second. Nothing starts on mount.

props.name: onSeek
props.description: Fires with a word's start time when it is clicked or activated.

props.name: onTimeChange
props.description: Fires on every tick, so a controlled parent can follow the clock.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the line for assistive technology.

usageNotes: Roving tabindex: Left and Right walk the words, Home and End jump to the ends, Enter or Space seeks to the focused word.
Under reduced motion each word switches colour at its moment — no sweep, no inflate, no travelling caret — because the timing is the information.
The clock parks at the last word's end; pass playing again after seeking back to run it a second time.

items.title: Transcript Flow
items.tagline: Tentative in grey, firm when it's sure.
items.description: A transcript that shows its own confidence. Words arrive tentative in muted ink and firm to foreground on a colour tween when their segment finalises, a word the recogniser revises cross-fades in place with the old copy popped out of flow so the line never doubles in width mid-swap, and new words enter from a nudge on glide. While the microphone is open a dot breathes at the end of the text on drift, the slowest spring in the set, because ambient state should not compete with the words. The view follows the speaker only while the reader is already at the bottom, with one button back to the live edge; the region is a focusable log the keyboard can scroll, and finalised text is announced through a polite status instead of the live edge. Under reduced motion the pulse holds still and the colours simply swap.

props.name: segments
props.type: { id: string; text: string; final: boolean }[]
props.description: The transcript so far, oldest first. Replace a segment's text to revise it in place.

props.name: listening
props.description: Shows the breathing pulse at the end of the text.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Scroll height in pixels. The box grows to it and no further.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the log for assistive technology.

usageNotes: The log is focusable, so the keyboard can scroll it; scrolling up pins the view and the Latest button returns to the live edge.
Under reduced motion the pulse holds still, words appear without travel, and tentative text still swaps colour when it firms.
Only finalised segments are announced — the live edge is aria-live off, or every revision would be read aloud.

items.title: Unit Flip
items.tagline: Flip the unit; the digits re-roll.
items.description: A readout whose unit is the control. Pressing the chip turns it over — rotateX on snap, two faces on one card, one crisp overshoot as it lands — while the digits re-roll to the converted value, each glyph riding out of its own slot in the direction of the flip so the number reads as re-measured rather than replaced. Precision follows the unit, so the miles reading keeps two decimals where the kilometres reading keeps one. The chip is a button carrying aria-pressed, Space and Enter flip it, its accessible name says which unit is showing and which is a press away, and the converted value is announced through a polite status. Under reduced motion the card does not turn and the digits swap in place, because the reading is the information.

props.name: value
props.description: The measurement, expressed in the first unit.

props.name: units
props.description: The pair — { label, convert, digits } — each converting from the base value.

props.name: unit / defaultUnit
props.description: Controlled or initial unit index.

props.name: onUnitChange
props.description: Fires on flip with the index now showing.

props.name: label
props.description: What is being measured; sits opposite the readout and truncates rather than wrapping.

usageNotes: The unit chip is a button with aria-pressed: Space or Enter flips it, and its accessible name names both the current unit and the one a press away.
Under reduced motion the card does not turn and the digits swap in place — the converted reading still changes.
Decimal places come from each unit's digits (default 1), so a coarse unit and a fine one can read at their own precision.

items.title: Reorder List
items.tagline: Lift a row; the others make room.
items.description: A list you rearrange by hand. The row under the pointer lifts to 1.02 with a raised edge on flick and then tracks the pointer 1:1, while the rows it passes slide out of its way on glide and the drop settles it into its slot on snap. The pointer is captured only after 4px of travel, so a plain tap still lands; Space lifts the focused row, Up and Down move it, Home and End send it to the ends, Space drops and Escape puts it back, with every step announced politely.

props.name: items
props.type: { id: string; label: string; meta?: string }[]
props.description: Seeds the order; the list owns it after that and reports through onReorder.

props.name: onReorder
props.description: Fires with the whole list once a row is dropped, never mid-move.

props.name: renderItem
props.description: Replaces the row's content. Rows keep one shared height either way, so the drop target stays unambiguous.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible list label; names the list for assistive technology.

usageNotes: Space lifts the focused row, Up and Down move it, Home and End send it to the ends, Space drops it and Escape restores the order it started from. Each step is announced in a polite live region.
The pointer is captured only after 4px of travel, so a tap on a row is never swallowed by the drag.
Under reduced motion nothing travels: rows swap places as the pointer crosses them, because the order is the information.

items.title: Agenda Day
items.tagline: Events stack in the day; now creeps down the column.
items.description: A day drawn on its hours. Events arrive a step from the gutter in cascade order on glide, overlapping events share the column and re-divide it as one is moved out of the pile, and the now-line creeps down on drift from the now prop rather than the wall clock so the day renders the same on the server as in the browser. Dragging a block tracks the pointer 1:1 and settles onto its quarter hour on snap; Up and Down move the focused event a quarter hour, Page Up and Page Down an hour, and every move is announced.

props.name: events
props.type: { id: string; title: string; start: number; end: number; tint?: string }[]
props.description: Minutes from the start of the day. Seeds the agenda, which owns positions after that and reports via onChange.

props.name: hours
props.description: Visible range as whole hours. Ten hours fit a 342px phone column without a scroll.

props.name: now
props.description: Minutes for the now-line. Omit it, or send it out of range, and no line is drawn.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fires with the whole day after a drop or a keyboard nudge.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.description: Fires with the focused event id, or null when focus leaves the day.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label. Omit it and pass aria-label to name the day invisibly.

usageNotes: Every event is a button whose name reads its title and both times. Up and Down move the focused event a quarter hour, Page Up and Page Down an hour, Left and Right walk between events, Home and End jump to the ends; each move is announced politely.
The pointer is captured only after 4px of travel, and the grid re-divides its columns in quarter-hour steps while the block itself follows the pointer.
The now-line is driven by the now prop, never Date.now(), so the first client paint matches the server's markup.
Under reduced motion events appear without travel and land instantly; the times still change, because the time is the information.

items.title: Lane Board
items.tagline: Cards cross lanes; the columns make room.
items.description: A board whose columns make room. Lifting a card takes it out of its lane on flick, the lane under the pointer opens a placeholder of exactly that card's height which travels between lanes on glide while the cards around it re-flow, and letting go settles the card from where the hand left it into the slot on snap as both lanes' counts roll. The pointer is captured only after 4px of travel, and every card is a menu button whose four moves — a lane left, a lane right, a place up, a place down — are reachable from the keyboard and announced.

props.name: lanes
props.type: { id: string; title: string; cards: { id: string; title: string; tag?: string }[] }[]
props.description: Seeds the board; it owns card placement after that and reports via onMove.

props.name: onMove
props.type: (cardId: string, toLane: string, index: number) => void
props.description: Fires on a drop or a keyboard move, with the index the card landed on.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible board label. Omit it and pass aria-label to name the board invisibly.

usageNotes: Every card is a menu button: Enter or Space opens its four moves, arrow keys walk them past the ones that are unavailable, Escape closes, and each landing is announced politely with its lane and position.
The pointer is captured only after 4px of travel, and the drop target is read from lane bands measured once as the drag engages, so the placeholder never hunts between two slots.
Lanes scroll sideways under edge fades when the board is wider than its column; three lanes fit the doc width.
Under reduced motion nothing travels: the card stays put and marked while the placeholder shows where it will land.

items.title: Unfold Card
items.tagline: The card unfolds into its detail in place.
items.description: A list of cards that open where they stand. Clicking one unfolds its detail directly beneath its summary, the container animating to a height a ResizeObserver actually measured on glide, so nothing is reserved while the card is folded and nothing below it jumps when it opens; the cards that stay folded ease back in opacity, a lighting change rather than a movement, and the chevron turns on snap. Only one card is open at a time, each summary is a button carrying aria-expanded and aria-controls, and Escape folds the open card and returns focus to its summary.

props.name: items
props.type: { id: string; summary: React.ReactNode; detail: React.ReactNode }[]
props.description: The cards, in reading order. The summary is always visible; the detail is revealed beneath it.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial open id; null folds everything.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires with the id that opened, or null when everything folds.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible list label. Omit it and pass aria-label to name the list invisibly.

usageNotes: Each summary is a button carrying aria-expanded and aria-controls over a labelled region. Up and Down walk the cards, Home and End jump to the ends, Escape folds the open card and returns focus to its summary.
The open height is measured with a ResizeObserver rather than reserved, so a detail that grows in place carries the container with it.
Under reduced motion the detail swaps in at its natural height and the chevron turns instantly; the detail still appears, because the detail is the information.

items.title: Fit Panel
items.tagline: The panel's height follows its content.
items.description: A container that is exactly as tall as what is inside it. Swap the content by changing contentKey and the outgoing copy fades away on the exit ease, the incoming fades in, and the box glides between the two measured heights on glide, so nothing below the panel jumps and nothing above it is held open by a reserve. A ResizeObserver rides the mounted content, attached by the callback ref rather than an effect, so content that grows in place carries the panel with it.

props.name: children
props.description: Content; change contentKey to swap it.

props.name: contentKey
props.description: Identifies the current content. A new value fades the old copy out, the new one in, and glides the height between them.

props.name: onHeightChange
props.description: Fires with each freshly measured height, in pixels.

props.name: className
props.description: Outer classes. Padding belongs on the content, not on the panel.

usageNotes: A pure layout utility: it adds no roles of its own, so whatever semantics the content needs — a tabpanel, a region, a status — it brings with it.
The height is measured, never reserved, so the panel is never propped open for a state it is not showing.
Under reduced motion the height becomes the new height at once and the content swaps, because the content is the information.

items.title: Density Grid
items.tagline: Comfortable to compact; the rows tighten in place.
items.description: A members table with a density switch. Changing density is a layout animation on glide: rows are keyed by id, so each one keeps its identity and tightens in place — height, gutters and avatar closing at once — rather than the table reprinting itself at a new size. The switch is a radio group where Left and Right step between the three stops without wrapping, Home and End jump to comfortable and compact, and Space selects.

props.name: rows
props.type: { id: string; name: string; role: string; status: string }[]
props.description: Rows in reading order. The id keys the row, so it survives a density change as the same row.

props.name: density / defaultDensity
props.description: Controlled or initial row density.

props.name: onDensityChange
props.description: Fires when the switch moves, from the pointer or the keyboard.

props.name: columns
props.description: Column headers, left to right.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible table label. Omit it and pass aria-label to name the table invisibly.

usageNotes: The switch is a radio group with a roving tabindex: Left and Right step between comfortable, cozy and compact without wrapping past the ends, Home and End jump to the two extremes, Space selects.
Rows keep their keys, so the density change is a FLIP: each row tightens where it stands and the card follows it down, instead of the table reprinting at a new size.
The table scrolls inside its own overflow-x-auto box below its minimum width, so a phone column never pushes the page sideways.
Under reduced motion the sizes swap without travel — the table is still denser, it just does not animate there.

items.title: Summary Hem
items.tagline: The summary condenses as you scroll.
items.description: A sticky summary that pays for its own space. At rest it is a card of lines, total and action; scrolling the container down condenses it to a slim bar on glide, keeping the total and the button as the same travelling elements while only the itemised lines cross-fade. Scrolling back up reopens it, and the heading holds a disclosure button so Enter or Space does the same from the keyboard.

props.name: container
props.description: The scrolling element the hem listens to. The hem sits over it, not inside it.

props.name: lines
props.description: Itemised lines. They are what the condensed bar gives up.

props.name: total
props.description: Formatted total. Kept in both states, as one element that travels.

props.name: cta
props.description: The action. Kept in both states; full width expanded, beside the total when condensed.

props.name: heading
props.description: Names the region and the disclosure button.

props.name: onCondensedChange
props.description: Fires when the hem condenses or expands, whatever caused it.

usageNotes: The heading holds a disclosure button: Enter or Space expands and collapses the hem, aria-expanded reports the state and aria-controls points at the lines. Tab reaches the button and then the action.
Direction drives the condense, not a hard scroll position: scrolling down past a 4px deadzone condenses, scrolling up expands, and the top of the list is always the expanded state.
Place the hem inside a position: relative wrapper around the scrolling element and give the scroller bottom padding, so the last row can clear the bar.
Under reduced motion the two states swap without travel; the total and the action still change places, they just do not glide.

items.title: Step Slide
items.tagline: Steps slide by direction; the height fits.
items.description: A wizard whose frame fits the step it is showing. Next takes the current panel out to the left on the exit ease while the next arrives from a shift to the right on snap, Back reverses both, and the frame's height glides to the panel's measured height rather than reserving room for the tallest one. The dots fill in order and the current one stretches into a pill on snap; Back and Next are ordinary buttons and every move is announced politely.

props.name: steps
props.type: { id: string; title: string; content: React.ReactNode }[]
props.description: Ordered steps. Each renders as a group panel titled by its own heading.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial step index, clamped to the range.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires on every move, forwards or back.

props.name: onFinish
props.description: Fires when the forward button is pressed on the last step.

props.name: finishLabel
props.description: Label the forward button takes on the last step.

usageNotes: Back and Next are real buttons in one row: Back is disabled on the first step, Next reads Finish on the last, and each move is announced politely as its step number and title.
The frame's height is measured with a ResizeObserver on the live panel and glided to, never reserved — a short step is short and a tall one is never clipped.
Direction is carried into the panel variants, so a step always leaves the way you came from and arrives from the way you are headed.
Under reduced motion the panels cross-fade in place and the height swaps; the step still changes, it just does not travel.

items.title: Swipe Row
items.tagline: Swipe the row; the actions wait underneath.
items.description: A list row with its actions parked underneath. Dragging moves the row 1:1 with the pointer until it passes the open stop, then resists; crossing the overswipe threshold arms the first action, which grows on flick, and releasing runs it. Release settles on snap. The pointer is claimed only after 4px of horizontal travel and stands down when the travel is vertical, and every action is also in the row's menu, where Arrow keys move, Home and End jump and Escape returns focus.

props.name: leading / trailing
props.type: { id: string; label: string; icon: string; tone?: "neutral" | "danger"; onSelect: () => void }[]
props.description: Actions on each side. Leading is revealed by dragging right, trailing by dragging left; the first of a side is what an overswipe runs.

props.name: threshold
props.description: Fraction of the row's width that arms the first action.

props.name: children
props.description: Row content. It rides the drag; the menu button sits beside it.

props.name: menuLabel
props.description: Names the menu button that carries the same actions to the keyboard.

usageNotes: The menu button is the keyboard path: it opens a menu of every action, where Arrow keys move, Home and End jump, Enter or Space selects and Escape closes and returns focus to the button. The swipe panes are aria-hidden and out of the tab order so a row never costs three tab stops.
The pointer is captured only after 4px of horizontal travel and the gesture stands down entirely when the travel is vertical, so a tap stays a tap and the list still scrolls under the thumb.
Render each row inside a ul or ol — the component's root is an li. An open row closes on the next press anywhere else on the page.
Under reduced motion the row reveals and closes without springs; the actions still appear, they just do not overshoot.

items.title: Shrink Bar
items.tagline: The header compacts as you go.
items.description: A header that spends its height as you scroll. One progress value, read straight off the container's scrollTop over the first range pixels, drives the bar's height, the title's scale and the subtitle's fold — scroll-linked with no spring anywhere, because a header that keeps moving after your finger stops reads as lag. The title is a single element throughout, so assistive technology sees one heading rather than a large copy handing over to a small one.

props.name: container
props.description: The scrolling element the bar reads. The bar sits over it, never inside its flow.

props.name: title / subtitle
props.description: Header copy. The title is one element in both states; the subtitle folds away as the bar compacts.

props.name: range
props.description: Scroll pixels over which the bar compacts fully.

props.name: actions
props.description: Right-side controls, centred on the bar at every height.

props.name: onCompactionChange
props.description: Fires with the compaction percent, reported in fives so a fling does not re-render the host every frame.

usageNotes: Place the bar inside a position: relative wrapper around the scrolling element and offset the scroller's top padding by SHRINK_BAR_HEIGHT.rest, which the component exports. Keeping the bar out of flow is what stops a shrinking header from shortening the document under the reader's own scroll.
The compaction is a scroll-linked transform with no spring: the bar is exactly where the scroll says it should be, and reverses the instant the scroll does.
The title is one h2 that scales toward its left edge and travels up as the bar closes around it, so the heading is never duplicated for the two states.
Under reduced motion the progress snaps at the halfway mark: the bar switches between its two states rather than tracking the scroll.

items.title: Side Scroll
items.tagline: Scroll down; the track moves across.
items.description: A section that pins itself while the track inside it moves sideways. The container's vertical travel maps linearly onto the track's horizontal travel — deliberately no spring, because a scroll-linked value that springs lags the finger and reads as jank — and the section reserves exactly its frame height plus the track's travel, so the pin lasts as long as there is track left. Native scroll means Page Down and the arrow keys already work, and a skip control at the top of the pin jumps a keyboard past the run and lands focus on the far side.

props.name: panels
props.description: The panels, left to right.

props.name: container
props.description: The scrolling element whose travel drives the track.

props.name: panelWidth
props.description: Width of one panel, px.

props.name: onProgressChange
props.description: Fires with whole-percent progress, 0–100, when the percent changes.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the pinned section.

props.name: skipLabel
props.description: Text of the control that jumps past the pinned run.

usageNotes: The track rides native scroll, so Page Down, Space and the arrow keys move it with no key handling of its own; a skip control, visible once focused, scrolls past the pin and moves focus to a target on the far side of it.
Under reduced motion the panels stack into a column and scroll the ordinary way — the progress rail still fills, because progress is information rather than flourish.
The section reserves frame height plus track travel, so give the container enough room after it; the track clips inside its own frame and never overflows the page.

items.title: Snap Carousel
items.tagline: Snaps to the slide; the dot becomes a pill.
items.description: A carousel on native scroll-snap, so the gesture is the browser's own and the component only decides where it lands. The dot for the settled slide stretches into a pill on snap — a layout animation, so one shape travels and widens rather than a second dot blinking on elsewhere — while the next slide peeks past the edge. Autoplay is a chain of timeouts keyed to the settled index, standing down on hover, on focus inside the carousel and whenever the tab is hidden; the scroller is focusable, Left and Right move a slide, Home and End jump, and the dots carry a roving tabindex.

props.name: slides
props.description: Slides, left to right.

props.name: autoplay
props.description: Milliseconds between advances; omit to disable autoplay.

props.name: loop
props.description: Wrap past the ends.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the carousel.

props.name: onIndexChange
props.description: Fires when the settled slide changes.

usageNotes: The scroller is focusable: Left and Right move one slide, Home and End jump to the ends. The dots are a roving tabindex — arrows move and select, and the settled dot carries aria-current.

Autoplay pauses on hover, on focus inside the carousel and while the tab is hidden, and a visible toggle stops it outright; the live slide count falls silent while it is rotating so it never talks over the reader.
Under reduced motion autoplay never starts, the dots swap rather than stretching, and moving between slides jumps instead of scrolling.

items.title: Hover Preview
items.tagline: Hover the card; it plays its frames.
items.description: A card that plays its own frames while you are looking at it. One linear driver runs from zero to the frame count and back on a loop: its floor picks the frame, so the card re-renders once per frame rather than once per tick, and the same value feeds the hairline under the art, which is why the bar and the picture can never disagree. Hovering with a mouse or reaching the card with the keyboard starts a pass and leaving falls back to the poster on the exit ease; a press pins playback, which is what a tap does on touch, so it is a real toggle button with aria-pressed that Enter and Space operate.

props.name: frames
props.description: How many frames the sequence has.

props.name: renderFrame
props.description: Draws frame index; index 0 is the poster.

props.name: duration
props.description: Length of one pass through the sequence, ms.

props.name: title
props.description: Card title, and the control's accessible name.

props.name: onPlayingChange
props.description: Fires when this card starts or stops playing.

usageNotes: A toggle button: Tab reaches it, keyboard focus starts a pass, Enter and Space pin playback, and aria-pressed reports whether it is pinned — which is also what a tap does on touch.
Playback stops while the tab is hidden and resumes when it comes back, so a grid of cards costs nothing behind another window.
Under reduced motion the card is a still: the poster, a Preview badge and no playback — and no control either, since there is no longer a gesture the keyboard would need to match.

items.title: Grab Pan
items.tagline: Grab the board; throw it; it bounces at the edges.
items.description: A board you grab and throw. The drag is one-to-one with the pointer and follows at a third of the travel past an edge, so the end of the board is felt rather than announced; release hands the offset to a requestAnimationFrame loop that decays the release velocity against elapsed time, and the moment it touches a bound it hands over to glide for the last pixels back. Pointer capture waits for 4px so a click on the board is never swallowed, and every gesture has a keyboard equal: the viewport is focusable, arrows pan a fifth of the view on glide, and Home re-centres.

props.name: width / height
props.description: Board size in px.

props.name: children
props.description: What sits on the board.

props.name: minimap
props.description: Show the minimap.

props.name: viewportHeight
props.description: Height of the viewport the board is seen through, px.

props.name: onOffsetChange
props.description: Fires with the whole-pixel offset whenever it changes.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the pannable region.

props.name: resetLabel
props.description: Label of the re-centre control.

usageNotes: The viewport is focusable: arrow keys pan a fifth of the view on glide, Home re-centres, and a visible Reset control does the same with the mouse. The wheel pans, and declines the page's scroll only when the board still has somewhere to go.
Pointer capture is taken after 4px of travel, so a click on something sitting on the board is never swallowed, and a gesture that ends without capture leaves the board untouched.
Under reduced motion nothing is thrown and nothing rubber-bands: the board tracks the pointer, stops dead at the edges, and jumps to its keyboard steps.

items.title: Path Rider
items.tagline: It rides the path as you scroll.
items.description: Something that rides a path. One value between zero and one places the rider at that fraction of the path's length using the browser's own geometry — a point plus the two either side of it, which give the tangent it turns to — and the travelled part of the route draws in behind it from the same value through pathLength, so the line and the rider cannot disagree. Scroll-linked progress is mapped linearly from the container and never sprung, play runs the same value on a linear tween that pauses with the tab and resumes where it stopped, and the rider is hidden from assistive technology while the caption carries the position as text.

props.name: path
props.description: SVG path data the rider follows.

props.name: viewBox
props.description: The coordinate space the path is drawn in.

props.name: progress
props.description: Controlled position along the path, 0–1. Omit to follow the container.

props.name: container
props.description: Scroll-link source; used when progress is omitted.

props.name: rider
props.description: What travels. Defaults to a chevron badge.

props.name: playing
props.description: Runs progress to the end on a linear tween.

props.name: duration
props.description: Length of a full run, ms.

props.name: onProgressChange
props.description: Fires with progress, 0–1, whenever the whole percent changes.

props.name: onPlayEnd
props.description: Fires when a run reaches the end.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the route in the caption.

usageNotes: The rider is decorative and aria-hidden; position is exposed as text in the caption, so drive it from a control that carries its own semantics — a native range input, or the container's scroll.
Progress has one source at a time: playing wins, then a controlled progress prop, then the container's scroll. Scroll mapping is linear on purpose — a spring on a scroll-linked value lags the finger.
Under reduced motion a run advances in eight jumps instead of gliding, so the trip still finishes and still reports; scrubbed and scroll-linked progress place the rider without travel either way.

items.title: Live Rows
items.tagline: New rows arrive; old ones leave; the list keeps its feet.
items.description: A live feed that keeps its feet. A row arrives from a step above and glides the rest of the list down on the glide spring — a layout move, so the rows below travel rather than jump — while a cobalt wash drains off the new row and is cool by the time the next one lands; rows pushed past max fade and collapse on the exit ease. The list holds while a pointer is over it or the keyboard is inside it, so arrivals queue and land together on release, and Tab reaches anything a row contains without the feed moving underneath.

props.name: items
props.description: Rows, newest first. Ids must be stable — the row travels on its key rather than remounting.

props.name: max
props.description: Rows kept on screen; anything past it collapses out on the exit ease.

props.name: paused
props.description: Holds the list from outside: arrivals wait, removals still land.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the log region and titles the header beside the live indicator.

props.name: emptyLabel
props.description: Read in place of the rows while the feed is empty.

props.name: onHoldChange
props.description: Fires when a pointer or a focus enters and leaves the list, so a host can narrate the hold.

usageNotes: Focus holds the list exactly as hover does, so Tab can reach a control inside a row without the feed sliding out from under it; the header states Live or Held in plain text rather than colour alone.
Under reduced motion rows appear and vanish on opacity alone — no slide, no collapse — because the arrivals are the information and are never animated away.
The frame is a polite log region announcing additions once. A held list still honours removals, so clearing items empties the display even while the hold is on.

items.title: Tap Ripple
items.tagline: A ripple from where you pressed.
items.description: A press ripple that starts where the press did. On pointerdown a disc is placed under the finger and expands on a tween over durations.slow — a spreading front, not a landing, so it never springs — sized from the press point to the furthest corner so it always covers the surface, and it fades on the exit ease when the press is let go. Enter and Space ripple from the centre because a keyboard press has no point to start from, and the wrapper clones the button rather than boxing it, so role, label, disabled state and handlers are exactly what the caller wrote.

props.name: color
props.description: Ripple colour, used at full strength. Left out, the disc is currentColor at 16%.

props.name: duration
props.description: Expansion in milliseconds; the fade on release runs on the base tween regardless.

props.name: children
props.description: The button. It is cloned, not wrapped: it keeps its own classes, handlers and semantics.

usageNotes: Enter and Space ripple from the centre, and a key held while focus moves away is released on blur so no disc is left behind.
Under reduced motion nothing travels: the surface takes a brief wash on the exit ease instead of an expanding disc.
The ripple layer is aria-hidden, takes no pointer events, and inherits the button's own border radius, so it clips exactly to the corner the caller drew.

items.title: Badge Bump
items.tagline: The count bumps when it changes.
items.description: A count badge that reacts to its own number. Every change bumps the pill from 1.25 back to 1 on recoil — two visible bounces, the physics of something landing — while the digits roll on snap and a wash of the badge's own ink flashes and drains on the exit ease. Going to zero is not a bump: the badge shrinks away on the exit ease, and a polite status line carries the count so the host button keeps whatever name it already had.

props.name: count
props.description: The number. Zero collapses the badge on the exit ease rather than bumping it.

props.name: max
props.description: Cap; anything above it reads as 99+ and stops the badge growing.

props.name: tone
props.description: Colour. The wash uses the badge's own ink, so every tone flashes correctly.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the number for assistive technology — the status line reads "12 unread".

props.name: children
props.description: The thing the badge sits on, usually an icon button.

usageNotes: The badge is aria-hidden decoration; the count is announced once per change by a polite status line, so the host button keeps its own accessible name and nothing is said twice.
Under reduced motion the digits swap instantly and the badge does not bump — the wash still flashes, because the new number is information.
The bump runs imperatively as a two-keyframe spring, which is the only shape a spring can take; the digit stack stays mounted underneath so the outgoing number rolls out rather than disappearing.

items.title: Morph Icon
items.tagline: One icon becomes the other, path by path.
items.description: Icons that become each other rather than swapping. Five built-in pairs — play/pause, menu/close, plus/cross, heart, sun/moon — are each drawn twice with matching commands and point counts, so motion interpolates the d attribute directly and every corner travels to its counterpart on snap, one crisp overshoot arriving at the shape it means. The control is a real toggle button: aria-pressed carries the state, the accessible name swaps with it, and Enter and Space work because nothing was reinvented.

props.name: pair
props.description: Which morph. Each pair ships both shapes with the same commands and point count.

props.name: pressed / defaultPressed
props.description: Controlled or initial state; aria-pressed tracks it either way.

props.name: onPressedChange
props.description: Fires on toggle, after the internal state has moved.

props.name: labels
props.description: Accessible names for the two states; each pair carries a sensible default.

props.name: size
props.description: Icon size in pixels. The button pads around it, so the hit target grows with it.

usageNotes: A native toggle button: Tab reaches it, Enter and Space press it, aria-pressed carries the state and the accessible name swaps with it.
Under reduced motion the icons swap outright — the state is the information, the morph is only the manner.
Adding a pair means drawing both shapes with identical commands in identical order; where a stroke has nowhere to go, retreat it to a point and fade it rather than leaving a dot under a round cap.

items.title: Scroll Frames
items.tagline: Scroll scrubs the sequence.
items.description: A frame sequence scrubbed by scroll. The stage pins to the top of its container while a tall spacer scrolls past underneath, and the fraction already gone picks the frame — linearly, because a scrub has no physics of its own and any easing laid over it would fight the finger. Frames are drawn rather than loaded: renderFrame is handed a context already scaled to the display and sized by a ResizeObserver, and the sequence redraws itself when the box or the theme changes.

props.name: frames
props.description: Frame count. The last frame owns the final sliver, so a fully scrolled stage lands on the end.

props.name: renderFrame
props.type: (index: number, ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D, size: { w: number; h: number }) => void
props.description: Draws one frame in logical pixels; the retina scale and the clear are already done.

props.name: container
props.description: The scrolling element the stage is pinned inside — never the window.

props.name: height
props.description: Scroll distance the sequence is spread over. Minus the container's height, this is the scrub.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the canvas, which is exposed as an image.

props.name: onFrameChange
props.description: Fires with the frame index whenever it changes, from scroll and from the reduced-motion scrubber alike.

usageNotes: Scrolling is the container's own, so give that container tabIndex 0 and a name: arrows, Page keys and Home/End then scrub the sequence with no extra key handling.

Under reduced motion nothing is pinned and nothing moves on its own — the stage shows the final frame at its natural height with a native range input under it, so the whole sequence can still be read.
Keep renderFrame referentially stable (useCallback) and pure: it is called on every frame change, resize and theme flip, and reading tokens off ctx.canvas keeps the drawing correct in both themes.

items.title: Cart Fly
items.tagline: The item flies to the cart; the cart catches it.
items.description: Add to cart, with the item making the trip. Pressing throws a ghost of the button's thumbnail along an arc to whatever cartRef points at — x on a linear tween, y through a lifted middle keyframe — and the flight's own onComplete calls onAdd, so the cart bumps on recoil because it caught something. The button confirms with a check drawn on flick, and Enter or Space runs the same path.

props.name: cartRef
props.description: The element the ghost flies to; its box is measured at press time.

props.name: thumbnail
props.description: The picture that flies — rendered in the button and again as the ghost.

props.name: onAdd
props.description: Fires when the flight lands, so the cart counts what arrived.

props.name: label
props.description: Button copy.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Locks the button; no flight leaves.

usageNotes: It is a plain button: Tab reaches it, Enter or Space adds, and the outcome is announced through a polite live region.
Under reduced motion nothing flies — onAdd fires on the press and the button still confirms, because the count is information rather than flourish.
Both boxes are measured inside the press handler, so a scrolled page or a moved cart still lands true; several ghosts may be in the air at once.

items.title: Zoom Gallery
items.tagline: Thumbnails swap the picture; hover zooms into it.
items.description: A product gallery with a loupe. Choosing a thumbnail cross-fades the frame while the arriving picture settles from a hair over full size on glide, and the selection ring travels between thumbnails on a shared layoutId; hovering the frame opens a scaled copy translated so the point under the pointer stays under it, clamped to the picture's edges. The thumbnails are a tablist — Left and Right swap pictures, Home and End jump — and a pressed Zoom button opens the pane centred for the keyboard, with Arrow keys panning and Escape closing.

props.name: images
props.type: { id: string; alt: string; art: React.ReactNode }[]
props.description: Pictures; art is rendered in the thumbnail, the frame, and the zoom pane.

props.name: zoom
props.description: Magnification of the zoom pane.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial active picture id.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires when another picture is chosen.

props.name: onZoomChange
props.description: Fires when the zoom pane opens or closes.

usageNotes: The thumbnails are a tablist with a roving tabindex: Left and Right swap pictures without wrapping past the ends, Home and End jump to the first and last.
The Zoom button is the keyboard's path into the pane — it opens centred, Arrow keys pan it by a tenth of the picture, and Escape closes it.
Under reduced motion pictures swap without travel and the pane holds still rather than following the pointer; the magnification itself still shows, because it is information.

items.title: Wave Scrub
items.tagline: Bars for the sound; the played part fills.
items.description: A scrubber that shows the sound. The played part is the same waveform in a second colour, revealed by a clip that chases the clock on a short linear tween — a spring would overshoot the present — and the elapsed readout is that same motion value formatted, so the digits roll with the fill. Dragging scrubs after 4px of travel, hovering floats the time under the pointer, the transport morphs between play and pause on snap, and Left and Right step five seconds on a slider whose aria-valuetext reads mm:ss.

props.name: peaks
props.description: Bar heights, 0–1, left to right.

props.name: duration
props.description: Length of the recording, in seconds.

props.name: position / defaultPosition
props.description: Controlled or initial position, in seconds played.

props.name: onSeek
props.description: Fires on every scrub, tap, and arrow press.

props.name: playing / defaultPlaying
props.description: Controlled or initial transport state.

props.name: onPlayingChange
props.description: Fires when the transport button is pressed.

usageNotes: The waveform is a slider: Left and Right step five seconds, Up and Down do the same, Home and End jump to the ends, and aria-valuetext reads mm:ss of mm:ss.
Pointer capture waits for 4px of travel, so a plain tap still seeks where it landed and a vertical touch keeps scrolling the page.
Under reduced motion the fill steps to each new position instead of gliding — the progress is information, only the travel is dropped. It plays no audio; drive position from your own clock.

items.title: Coupon Slot
items.tagline: The ticket tears; the total drops.
items.description: A coupon field shaped like the ticket it is. A code that takes tears the stub off along its perforation — a closing clip and a turn on the exit ease, because a tear accelerates away and never springs back — the seam's two halves part, a discount line glides in beneath the subtotal, and the total rolls down to meet it. A code that is refused nudges the field 4px and settles on recoil while the seam opens and reseals on that same spring; Enter applies, and the outcome is wired to the input through aria-describedby.

props.name: onApply
props.description: Validates a code and returns { label, amount }, or null to refuse it.

props.name: subtotal
props.description: The figure the discount comes off.

props.name: format
props.description: Money formatter; the component prints nothing this does not return.

props.name: label
props.description: Field label, shown above the stub.

props.name: onDiscountChange
props.description: Fires when a discount is applied or removed.

usageNotes: A plain input: Enter applies, Apply is disabled while the field is empty, and the outcome is both described by aria-describedby and announced through a live region that is already in the document.
Focus follows the work — to Remove when the stub tears off, back to the field when Remove puts it back.
Under reduced motion nothing travels: the discount line and the stub appear, the seam stays sealed, and the total's digits swap rather than roll.

items.title: Parcel Line
items.tagline: The parcel moves along the stops.
items.description: A delivery that shows its own progress. The parcel glides between stops on glide and is placed from measured dot centres rather than a percentage, so it lands true on whichever row the stops wrapped onto at phone width; the stop it sits on breathes on drift, a reversing two-keyframe spring, while passed stops fill in order on flick through a cascade that keeps the run inside the 600ms budget. The stops are an ordered list with aria-current on the one in hand, and the ETA rolls when it changes and is announced politely.

props.name: stops
props.type: { id: string; label: string; time?: string }[]
props.description: Ordered stops, first to last.

props.name: current
props.description: Index of the stop the parcel is at; clamped to the run.

props.name: eta
props.description: Formatted arrival, shown in the header and announced when it changes.

props.name: label
props.description: Shipment name; names the region and opens the announcement.

usageNotes: An ordered list, not a widget: aria-current marks the stop in hand, every other stop carries a hidden word of state, and the whole reading is announced through a polite live region.
Stops wrap into a second row at phone width and the parcel follows, because its position comes from measured dot centres rather than a percentage of the track.
Under reduced motion the parcel jumps to its stop and nothing breathes; the fills, the labels, and the ETA still change.

items.title: Tip Pick
items.tagline: Pick a tip; the total keeps up.
items.description: A tip selector that keeps the arithmetic visible. Choosing a chip slides one shared fill across to it on snap and rolls the tip and total digits in the direction the money moved. Custom unfolds an amount field on glide at a height a ResizeObserver measured, then moves focus into it; the chips are a radio group where arrows wrap, Home and End jump, and Enter or Space commits.

props.name: subtotal
props.description: Bill before tip; percentages are taken from it.

props.name: presets
props.description: Percentages offered as chips, before Custom and No tip.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.type: { kind: "percent"; value: number } | { kind: "amount"; value: number } | { kind: "none" }
props.description: Controlled or initial tip; defaults to the middle preset.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires on every chip change and on every keystroke in the custom field.

props.name: format
props.description: Money formatter — the control never invents a currency.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible group label, which also names the radio group.

usageNotes: A radio group with a roving tabindex: Left and Right wrap around the chips, Home and End jump to the ends, and Enter or Space commits. Committing Custom moves focus into the amount field; arrowing onto it only unfolds, so the arrow keys keep working.
Under reduced motion the fill swaps instantly and the digits cross-fade in place — the tip and total still change, because the figures are information rather than flourish.
The custom panel's height is measured by a ResizeObserver, so nothing reserves dead space while it is shut; the panel is inert when closed so Tab never lands in a hidden field.

items.title: Flip Card Form
items.tagline: Focus the security code; the card turns over.
items.description: A card form whose preview is the feedback. Typing the number, name and expiry writes them onto the face and the brand mark cross-fades as the prefix resolves; focusing the security code turns the card over on snap — a real rotateY with backface-visibility hidden inline on both faces — and blurring turns it home. The inputs are real and carry cc-number, cc-name, cc-exp and cc-csc, the preview is aria-hidden, and under reduced motion the card swaps faces instead of turning.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.type: { number: string; name: string; expiry: string; cvc: string }
props.description: Controlled or initial values; number, expiry and cvc are held as digits and grouped for display.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires on every keystroke with the sanitised values.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Fires on submit with the current values.

props.name: onSideChange
props.description: Fires when the preview turns over, so a page can narrate the side.

props.name: submitLabel
props.description: Submit button copy.

usageNotes: Four real inputs in tab order, each with its own label and autocomplete token, so a password manager fills the form; focusing the security code flips the card and blurring flips it home, which makes Tab the whole keyboard gesture.
Under reduced motion nothing rotates — the two faces swap on a short opacity tween, because which side you are on is information.
The preview is aria-hidden since it only repeats the fields; a polite live region announces which side is showing.

items.title: Shop Card
items.tagline: Hover shows the other angle; the add bar rises.
items.description: A product card that keeps its second thought below the fold. Hover or focus inside cross-fades the picture to its alternate view and raises the quick-add bar from under the frame on glide, at a height a ResizeObserver measured so nothing reserves space for it; the heart pops on two chained springs, out on flick and back on recoil, and choosing a variant rolls the price. It is an article with a real link for a title, the heart carries aria-pressed, and the variants are a radio group with a roving tabindex, so Tab alone raises the bar.

props.name: product
props.type: { id: string; title: string; price: number; variants: { id: string; label: string; price?: number }[]; art: [React.ReactNode, React.ReactNode] }
props.description: The product and its two views; a variant's own price overrides the product's.

props.name: onAdd
props.description: Fires from the quick-add bar with the chosen variant.

props.name: liked / defaultLiked
props.description: Controlled or initial wishlist state for the heart.

props.name: onLikedChange
props.description: Fires when the heart toggles.

props.name: href
props.description: Where the title link goes.

props.name: format
props.description: Money formatter — the card never invents a currency.

usageNotes: Tab into the card and the bar rises on focus-within: the variants are a radio group where arrows wrap and Home and End jump, the heart is a toggle button with aria-pressed, and quick add announces itself through a polite live region.
Under reduced motion the bar fades in where it sits and the heart never pops — the picture still cross-fades and the price still changes, because both are information.
A tap raises the bar on touch, where there is no hover; the bar is pointer-inert while it is down, so it never intercepts a click on the picture.

items.title: Record Hold
items.tagline: Hold to record; slide away to cancel.
items.description: A hold-to-record button that puts the discard where the thumb already is. Pressing grows a ring around the mic on snap and opens a pill carrying a live procedural waveform and a rolling timer; dragging left slides the mic with the pointer, tilts it toward a bin that swaps in for the record dot, and past cancelDistance the lid lifts so releasing discards on the exit ease. Releasing in place throws the pill clear on recoil as Sent lands behind it; Space or Enter toggles recording and Escape cancels.

props.name: onRecord
props.description: Lifecycle callback; seconds is the whole seconds held when the take ended.

props.name: maxSeconds
props.description: The take stops itself here, from inside the tick that crossed it.

props.name: cancelDistance
props.description: Pixels of leftward travel that arm the cancel and open the bin.

usageNotes: Space or Enter toggles recording and Escape cancels from anywhere while a take is live; the mic is a button with aria-pressed, and start, send and discard are announced through a polite live region.
Under reduced motion the waveform holds its profile instead of pulsing and the states swap without travel — the timer still counts, because elapsed time is information.
Pointer capture waits for 4px of travel so a plain press is never swallowed, and a release before the first tick is read as a tap rather than a one-frame take.

items.title: Crop Frame
items.tagline: Drag the frame; the thirds appear.
items.description: A crop frame that argues with its bounds. Dragging the frame or a corner fades in the rule-of-thirds grid and deepens the dim outside while the rect tracks the pointer 1:1; pushed past an edge the frame follows only a third of the way and springs home on glide. An aspect lock keeps the ratio, arrow keys nudge the frame and Shift and an arrow resize it, and x, y, width and height are four real sliders under the picture.

props.name: image
props.type: { width: number; height: number; art: React.ReactNode }
props.description: The picture in its own pixels; art fills the stage, which takes the same ratio.

props.name: aspect
props.description: Width over height. Omit for a free crop; set, it survives every drag, key and slider.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.type: { x: number; y: number; w: number; h: number }
props.description: Controlled or initial crop rect in image pixels; defaults to a centred 70% crop.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires with a rect that is always legal — clamped, on ratio, and inside the picture.

usageNotes: The frame takes focus: arrow keys move it, Shift and an arrow resize it, and Alt steps a single pixel. Below the picture the same rect is four sliders — crop left, top, width and height — each with arrows, Home and End.
Under reduced motion there is no rubber band: the frame stops at the edge and the grid and dim still change, because where the crop is remains information.
Pointer capture waits for 4px of travel so a plain click is never swallowed, and the rubber band is a visual offset only — the committed rect never leaves the picture.

items.title: Balance Roll
items.tagline: The number lands before the confetti would.
items.description: A balance whose digit columns roll to the new figure on glide, in a cascade that starts at the units and ripples left the way an odometer's small wheels stop first. Each column is one eleven-face strip — the ten digits and a bullet — so pressing the figure rolls it to dots instead of swapping in a placeholder, and the separators only fade, which keeps the layout still. A change slides a delta chip in beside the figure on snap and takes it away on the exit ease; the press is an aria-pressed button whose name carries the amount, so Enter and Space mask it and no reader wades through the columns.

props.name: value
props.description: The balance in major units. Changing it rolls the digits and raises the delta chip.

props.name: label
props.description: What the figure is; labels the readout for assistive technology.

props.name: format
props.description: Turns an amount into its printed string. The default pins an explicit locale so server and client agree.

props.name: masked / defaultMasked
props.description: Controlled or initial mask state; masked rolls every digit on to a bullet.

props.name: onMaskedChange
props.description: Fires from the press that toggled the mask.

props.name: onValueSettle
props.description: Fires once per settled change, from the effect that observed it.

props.name: deltaHoldMs
props.description: Milliseconds the delta chip holds before it fades; 0 keeps it up.

props.name: caption
props.description: A quiet line under the figure — the account the balance belongs to.

usageNotes: The figure is a real toggle button: Tab reaches it, Enter and Space mask and reveal, and its accessible name carries the amount while the rolling columns stay hidden from assistive technology.
Under reduced motion the digits swap to their faces with no roll or stagger and the chip fades in place — the change is still shown, because a movement of balance is information.
Masking hides the delta chip as well: a hidden balance that still advertises its movement is not hidden.

items.title: Account Deck
items.tagline: Pick an account; the rest step back.
items.description: A horizontal deck of account cards where the pick lifts on snap and every other card recedes exactly one step, so the deck reads as two planes rather than a perspective trick. The strip centres the chosen card by animating a motion value's x on snap, seeded from a ResizeObserver so the first paint lands centred, and the balance under the deck rolls its digits on snap because the roll belongs to the pick that caused it. It is a radiogroup with a roving tabindex — Left and Right step, Home and End jump, Space selects — and a pointer drag steps the pick only after 4px of travel, capturing inside try/catch.

props.name: accounts
props.description: The accounts left to right: id, name, kind, an optional masked tail, and a balance.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial account id; defaults to the first account.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the click, key or drag step that changed the pick.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats the balance under the deck. The default pins an explicit locale so server and client agree.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible group label; omit it and pass aria-label to label the deck invisibly.

props.name: balanceLabel
props.description: The caption over the rolling figure.

usageNotes: A radiogroup with a roving tabindex: Left and Right (or Up and Down) step without wrapping past the ends, Home and End jump to the outer accounts, Space selects the focused card.
Dragging steps the pick — travel under 4px is ignored so plain clicks survive, and each further 48px commits one step and re-anchors, so a long sweep walks the deck.
Under reduced motion nothing lifts or scales — the pick is carried by its rail, border and wash — the strip jumps to the centred position and the balance's digits swap.

items.title: Ledger Line
items.tagline: Every entry knows where it came from.
items.description: A transaction row that opens where it stands: pressing expands its merchant, category, running balance and reference on glide to a height a ResizeObserver measured, with the facts arriving on a cascade and the chevron turning on snap. A pending entry sweeps a soft band along its amount on a linear tween driven entirely by the status prop, and a settling entry stamps a tick that draws itself with pathLength on flick and lands from 1.3x on recoil. The row is a real aria-expanded button — Enter and Space toggle, Escape closes — and pending is a word and a hatch, never colour alone.

props.name: title
props.description: What the entry says on the statement.

props.name: amount
props.description: Signed major units; negative is a debit and the row composes the sign itself.

props.name: date
props.description: An already-formatted day label, so the row never reads a clock.

props.name: status
props.description: Pending shimmers along the amount; settling stamps the tick.

props.name: merchant
props.description: The resolved merchant line in the detail.

props.name: category
props.description: Category chip in the detail; its dot sits on the label's centreline.

props.name: runningBalance
props.description: Balance after this entry; omitted, the line is left out.

props.name: reference
props.description: Reference code in the detail.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial expansion.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the press or the Escape that changed it.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats an unsigned amount. The default pins an explicit locale so server and client agree.

usageNotes: The row is a real button carrying aria-expanded and aria-controls: Enter and Space toggle the detail, Escape closes it and leaves focus on the row.
The panel's height is measured with a ResizeObserver rather than reserved, so a row with fewer facts is shorter instead of padded.
Under reduced motion nothing sweeps and nothing stamps: pending shows a hatched chip, the tick appears complete, and the panel opens instantly with the facts fading in.

items.title: Running Tally
items.tagline: Deposits climb, withdrawals sink, the total keeps up.
items.description: A movements list where each new entry arrives from the side its sign points to — a credit from the right, a debit from the left, on snap — while the list makes room by animating its height on glide, so the rows below are pushed rather than teleported. The total rolls its digits on glide and a hairline under it wipes toward the side the movement came from before fading, which is the instrument's only celebration: a withdrawal gets the same physics as a deposit, in the other direction.
